https://docs.example.com/docs/api/authen.markdown:
On this page

All API requests require authentication using an API key.

## API Keys[​](#api-keys "Direct link to API Keys")

API keys are used to authenticate requests to our API. You can manage your API keys in the [dashboard](https://dashboard.example.com).

### Creating an API Key[​](#creating-an-api-key "Direct link to Creating an API Key")

1. Log in to your dashboard
2. Navigate to **Settings** > **API Keys**
3. Click **Create New Key**
4. Give your key a descriptive name
5. Copy and securely store the key (it won't be shown again)

### Key Types[​](#key-types "Direct link to Key Types")

| Type     | Description                 | Use Case               |
| -------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| **Test** | For development and testing | Sandbox environment    |
| **Live** | For production use          | Production environment |

## Using API Keys[​](#using-api-keys "Direct link to Using API Keys")

Include your API key in the `Authorization` header:

```
curl https://api.example.com/v1/users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
```

Or using the SDK:

```
const client = new Client({
  apiKey: 'your-api-key',
});
```

## OAuth Configuration[​](#oauth-configuration "Direct link to OAuth Configuration")

For applications that need to act on behalf of users, we support OAuth 2.0.

### OAuth Flow[​](#oauth-flow "Direct link to OAuth Flow")

1. Redirect user to authorization URL
2. User grants permission
3. Receive authorization code
4. Exchange code for access token
5. Use access token for API requests

### Implementation[​](#implementation "Direct link to Implementation")

```
import { OAuth } from '@example/sdk';

const oauth = new OAuth({
  clientId: 'your-client-id',
  clientSecret: 'your-client-secret',
  redirectUri: 'https://yourapp.com/callback',
});

// Generate authorization URL
const authUrl = oauth.getAuthorizationUrl({
  scopes: ['read', 'write'],
  state: 'random-state-string',
});

// Exchange code for token
const tokens = await oauth.exchangeCode(authorizationCode);
```

### Scopes[​](#scopes "Direct link to Scopes")

| Scope    | Description                   |
| -------- | ----------------------------- |
| `read`   | Read-only access to resources |
| `write`  | Create and modify resources   |
| `delete` | Delete resources              |
| `admin`  | Full administrative access    |

## Token Refresh[​](#token-refresh "Direct link to Token Refresh")

Access tokens expire after 1 hour. Use the refresh token to get a new access token:

```
const newTokens = await oauth.refreshToken(refreshToken);
```

## Security Best Practices[​](#security-best-practices "Direct link to Security Best Practices")

- Never expose API keys in client-side code
- Use environment variables for key storage
- Rotate keys periodically
- Use the minimum required scopes
- Monitor API key usage in your dashboard

## Users[​](#users "Direct link to Users")

### List Users[​](#list-users "Direct link to List Users")

Retrieve a paginated list of users.

```
GET /v1/users
```

**Query Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type    | Default | Description                            |
| --------- | ------- | ------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `page`    | integer | 1       | Page number                            |
| `limit`   | integer | 20      | Items per page (max 100)               |
| `status`  | string  | -       | Filter by status: `active`, `inactive` |

**Example Request:**

```
curl https://api.example.com/v1/users?limit=10 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
```

**Example Response:**

```
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "user_123",
      "email": "john@example.com",
      "name": "John Doe",
      "status": "active",
      "createdAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "page": 1,
    "limit": 10,
    "total": 42
  }
}
```

### Get User[​](#get-user "Direct link to Get User")

Retrieve a single user by ID.

```
GET /v1/users/:id
```

**Example Request:**

```
curl https://api.example.com/v1/users/user_123 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
```

### Create User[​](#create-user "Direct link to Create User")

Create a new user.

```
POST /v1/users
```

**Request Body:**

```
{
  "email": "jane@example.com",
  "name": "Jane Smith",
  "role": "member"
}
```

**Example Request:**

```
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/v1/users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "jane@example.com", "name": "Jane Smith"}'
```

### Update User[​](#update-user "Direct link to Update User")

Update an existing user.

```
PATCH /v1/users/:id
```

### Delete User[​](#delete-user "Direct link to Delete User")

Delete a user.

```
DELETE /v1/users/:id
```

## Projects[​](#projects "Direct link to Projects")

### List Projects[​](#list-projects "Direct link to List Projects")

```
GET /v1/projects
```

### Create Project[​](#create-project "Direct link to Create Project")

```
POST /v1/projects
```

**Request Body:**

```
{
  "name": "My Project",
  "description": "A sample project"
}
```

## Error Handling[​](#error-handling "Direct link to Error Handling")

All endpoints return errors in a consistent format:

```
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_request",
    "message": "The request was invalid",
    "details": {
      "field": "email",
      "issue": "Invalid email format"
    }
  }
}
```

### Error Codes[​](#error-codes "Direct link to Error Codes")

| Code              | HTTP Status | Description                |
| ----------------- | ----------- | -------------------------- |
| `unauthorized`    | 401         | Invalid or missing API key |
| `forbidden`       | 403         | Insufficient permissions   |
| `not_found`       | 404         | Resource not found         |
| `invalid_request` | 400         | Invalid request parameters |
| `rate_limited`    | 429         | Too many requests          |
| `server_error`    | 500         | Internal server error      |

## Rate Limiting[​](#rate-limiting "Direct link to Rate Limiting")

API requests are limited to:

- **100 requests per minute** for standard plans
- **1000 requests per minute** for enterprise plans

Rate limit headers are included in all responses:

```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 95
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1704067200
```

https://docs.example.com/docs/getting-st.markdown:
On this page

Learn how to configure the SDK for your use case.

## Basic Configuration[​](#basic-configuration "Direct link to Basic Configuration")

The simplest configuration requires only an API key:

```
import { Client } from '@example/sdk';

const client = new Client({
  apiKey: 'your-api-key',
});
```

## Advanced Options[​](#advanced-options "Direct link to Advanced Options")

For more control, you can specify additional options:

```
const client = new Client({
  apiKey: 'your-api-key',
  baseUrl: 'https://api.example.com/v2',
  timeout: 30000, // 30 seconds
  retries: 3,
  debug: true,
});
```

### Option Reference[​](#option-reference "Direct link to Option Reference")

| Option    | Type      | Default                      | Description              |
| --------- | --------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `apiKey`  | `string`  | required                     | Your API key             |
| `baseUrl` | `string`  | `https://api.example.com/v1` | API base URL             |
| `timeout` | `number`  | `10000`                      | Request timeout in ms    |
| `retries` | `number`  | `2`                          | Number of retry attempts |
| `debug`   | `boolean` | `false`                      | Enable debug logging     |

## Environment-Specific Configuration[​](#environment-specific-configuration "Direct link to Environment-Specific Configuration")

### Development[​](#development "Direct link to Development")

```
const client = new Client({
  apiKey: process.env.EXAMPLE_API_KEY,
  baseUrl: 'https://sandbox.example.com/v1',
  debug: true,
});
```

### Production[​](#production "Direct link to Production")

```
const client = new Client({
  apiKey: process.env.EXAMPLE_API_KEY,
  timeout: 5000,
  retries: 5,
});
```

## Logging[​](#logging "Direct link to Logging")

Enable detailed logging by setting `debug: true`:

```
const client = new Client({
  apiKey: 'your-api-key',
  debug: true,
});
```

This will log all requests and responses to the console.

## Next Steps[​](#next-steps "Direct link to Next Steps")

With configuration complete, check out the [API Reference](/docs/api/authentication) to start making requests.

https://docs.example.com/docs/getting-st.markdown:
On this page

This guide will walk you through installing our SDK in your project.

## Prerequisites[​](#prerequisites "Direct link to Prerequisites")

Before you begin, make sure you have:

- Node.js 18 or higher
- npm or yarn package manager
- A basic understanding of JavaScript/TypeScript

## Installing the SDK[​](#installing-the-sdk "Direct link to Installing the SDK")

Install the package using npm:

```
npm install @example/sdk
```

Or using yarn:

```
yarn add @example/sdk
```

## Verifying Installation[​](#verifying-installation "Direct link to Verifying Installation")

After installation, verify it works by importing the SDK:

```
import { Client } from '@example/sdk';

const client = new Client({
  apiKey: 'your-api-key',
});

console.log('SDK version:', client.version);
```

## Environment Variables[​](#environment-variables "Direct link to Environment Variables")

We recommend storing your API key in an environment variable:

```
export EXAMPLE_API_KEY=your-api-key
```

Then access it in your code:

```
const client = new Client({
  apiKey: process.env.EXAMPLE_API_KEY,
});
```

## Next Steps[​](#next-steps "Direct link to Next Steps")

Now that you have the SDK installed, proceed to [Configuration](/docs/getting-started/configuration) to set up your client.

https://docs.example.com/docs/intro.markdown:
On this page

Welcome to our Example Documentation! This site demonstrates how to use the `docusaurus-plugin-mcp-server` to expose your documentation to AI agents.

## What is MCP?[​](#what-is-mcp "Direct link to What is MCP?")

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that allows AI assistants to connect to external data sources. This plugin creates an MCP server from your Docusaurus documentation, allowing AI tools like Claude and Cursor to search and read your docs.

## Features[​](#features "Direct link to Features")

- **Full-text search** - AI agents can search across all your documentation
- **Page retrieval** - Get complete page content as clean markdown
- **Section extraction** - Extract specific sections by heading ID
- **Build-time processing** - All indexing happens during build, making runtime fast

## Quick Example[​](#quick-example "Direct link to Quick Example")

Once configured, AI agents can query your documentation like this:

```
Search for "authentication" in the docs
Get the page at /docs/api/authentication
Get the "oauth-configuration" section from the authentication page
```

## Next Steps[​](#next-steps "Direct link to Next Steps")

Head to [Installation](/docs/getting-started/installation) to get started!

https://docs.example.com/no-article.markdown:
# No Article Page

This page has no article element and no main element. All of its content sits inside a plain div so that the extractor has to fall back to a broader selector, such as the body, to find anything useful.

It includes a second paragraph so the total amount of text comfortably exceeds three hundred characters, which keeps it above any minimum content length threshold the extractor might apply to pages.
